card.name: Awa Odori
card.era: Bon festivities since 16th c.; named 'Awa Odori' in the Showa period (from 1926)
card.tagline: Japan's largest Bon dance - the 'Fool's Dance' of Tokushima
card.profile: Awa Odori is the largest dance festival in Japan, held 12-15 August as part of Obon in Tokushima Prefecture on Shikoku, where choreographed troupes called ren parade through the streets to shamisen, taiko, shinobue and kane (Wikipedia, Awa Dance Festival). It is nicknamed the 'Fool's Dance' after the chant 'the dancing fool and the watching fool are both fools, so why not dance?' Its citywide form is popularly traced to a 1586 celebration of the opening of Tokushima Castle by Lord Hachisuka Iemasa, though historians note this account first appeared in 1908; the dance grew out of the local Bon Odori tradition (Tokushima Prefecture; Japan Guide).
card.insight: Per Wikipedia, 'Awa Odori is the largest dance festival in Japan, attracting over 1.3 million tourists every year,' with the number of dancers reaching about 100,000.
